question.problem:
Given that 
$|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ a & b+2\end{aligned}|=8$,
find 
$|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ a+3 & b\end{aligned}|.$
question.worked_solution:
We "factor out" the given determinant from the determinant we would like to find:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ a+3 & b\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ a+3 & (b+2)-2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the linearity property of determinants, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ a+3 & (b+2)-2\end{aligned}| & ={{|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ a & b+2\end{aligned}|}_{⏟}}_{8}+|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =8+(-6+6) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
